features.name: senet-features/1
layout: 0-28: 1 if the mover has a piece on square 1-26, 28-30 (a column each, in order)
58-63: one-hot number of the mover's pieces borne off, 0-5
70: the mover's remaining distance, the sum of 31 - s over its squares s, divided by 100

split.definition: validation records: the first val_frac of the records in the order of numpy.random.default_rng(seed).permutation (of the NumPy version given); training records: the others; unseen positions: the validation records whose (me, opp) occurs in no training record, which are positions rare in the data; distinct_positions: the number of different (me, opp) among the training records, the validation records, the unseen ones and all the records

notes: Recorded after the fact by `distill --evaluate --record`: the errors are measured now, on the split of the seed and val_frac given here; the training settings were not recorded.

Trained on 2026-10-02 by an earlier version of this script; models/training/distill.log is its log. The log shows the architecture (72-512-256-128-1) and 12 epochs; it does not show the other settings, which were that version's defaults unless overridden: batch 16384, lr 2e-3, wd 1e-5, val_frac 0.02, seed 0. That version split the records as this one does, so the split here is the training split if val_frac and seed were the defaults.

The training log's final errors, which this evaluation reproduces: validation MAE 0.00055, RMSE 0.00087, max 0.0214. Its 12 epochs took 1,838 s on a shared machine: 49 to 65 s each for eight of them, 218 to 673 s for epochs 6 to 9.

The training data, runs/train.bin, is not in the repository. models/training/train.manifest.json is its manifest, the one that inputs.training_data names: `senet gen-data` with the settings recorded there makes the file byte for byte (checked by SHA-256 against the file the network was trained on).
